analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date and a paragraph on GLM5Next video handling. The base patch is at about lines 810-813 and 829 of head, and units 12 and 13 show the surrounding text at lines 1211-2035. The paragraph now says variable-frame-rate video is indexed rather than refused. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, matching the reference loader, and the processor-refusal wording changes accordingly. No code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache-key or billing behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. I reviewed the supplied surrounding text for any security-relevant doc drift. It covers prefill geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling, tool parsing and vision caps, and none of it is modified. The text still says media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture (permitsHybridCheckpoint), so the T-041 cross-tenant cache posture is not affected. It also says media caps and the GLM decoded-frame cap of 512 MiB and prepared-pixel cap of 28,532 visual tokens are unchanged. One residual question: the doc describes a behavioral change in the GLM5Next video processor that accepts variable-frame-rate video. The code change is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that decodeAsset still enforces the decoded-frame cap, the 2 FPS sampling bound and the track-count/duration limits for VFR tracks. Otherwise a crafted VFR file could inflate memory or frame counts (availability, T-050/TB-007 area). This is unverified, not a finding, because the doc states those bounds remain.
